plain_english_policy: Enactment of this bill would eliminate the common law requirement that a victim must die within one year and one day for an act to be prosecuted as criminal homicide in Alabama.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Prosecutors could charge individuals with murder or manslaughter even if there is a significant delay (longer than 365 days) between the initial harmful act and the resulting death of the victim. This removes a procedural defense that previously barred prosecution based solely on the passage of time.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representatives McDaniel, McLaughlin, McCutcheon and Sanderford affirmatively advanced this change to the criminal code.
evidence_quotes: "Under existing common law... for the purpose of criminal homicide, the death of the victim must occur within a year and a day after the act causing the death."
"This bill would provide that it would not be a bar to prosecution for criminal homicide if the acts constituting the offense occurred more than a year and a day before the death."
